explanation: The main character in the Book of Ruth, a Moabite woman who converts to Judaism and becomes an ancestor of King David.
Ruth's mother-in-law, an Israelite who returns to Bethlehem after losing her husband and two sons in Moab.
A wealthy relative of Naomi's deceased husband, who marries Ruth and becomes her kinsman-redeemer.
A close relative obligated to marry the widow of a deceased family member to continue his lineage and preserve his name.
The season when grain and other crops are gathered from the fields. Ruth works in Boaz's field during the harvest.
God's unmerited favor or love. Ruth experiences grace through Boaz's care and protection.
Faithfulness and reliability in a relationship, especially between people and God. Ruth's loyalty to Naomi and to God is central to the story.
A lifelong covenant between man and woman, where they become one in God's sight. The marriage of Ruth and Boaz leads to blessing and fruitfulness.
Material goods and possessions passed from one generation to another. Ruth's marriage to Boaz secures the inheritance for Naomi's family.
